Fit a latent-variable model via EM + Laplace approximation

Source: R/em_laplace.R
tulpa_em_laplace.Rd

Generic EM engine. Model packages provide callbacks for the E-step (latent variable posterior) and the M-step encoding (how to assemble submodel data from weights). Each M-step submodel block is fit independently via tulpa_laplace(); the engine reads family and offset per block so heterogeneous-family mixtures (e.g. a binomial zero submodel + poisson positive submodel for a hurdle model) work without engine changes.

Usage

tulpa_em_laplace(
  e_step,
  m_step_encode,
  spatial = NULL,
  re_list = list(),
  max_iter = 50L,
  tol = 1e-04,
  damping = 0.3,
  correction = c("auto", "mi", "gibbs", "none"),
  n_imputations = 20L,
  n_gibbs = 2000L,
  n_louis = 1000L,
  draw_z = NULL,
  m_step_extra = NULL,
  beta_prior = NULL,
  verbose = TRUE,
  log_complete = NULL,
  correction_control = list(),
  ...
)

Arguments

e_step

Callback: function(fits, ...) -> list(weights = numeric, ...). Called once per EM iteration with the current per-submodel tulpa_laplace() fits. Must return a list whose weights element is the latent-variable posterior used by the next M-step.

m_step_encode

Callback: function(weights, ...) -> list of blocks. Each block is itself a list with the following fields:

  • y (numeric, required) – response.

  • X (matrix, required) – fixed-effects design with nrow(X) == length(y).

  • family (character scalar, required) – one of "binomial", "poisson", "gaussian", "negbin" / "neg_binomial_2", "gamma", "beta". Forwarded to tulpa_laplace() for that block.

  • n_trials (numeric or NULL, optional; absent or NULL defaults to 1) – binomial trial counts.

  • offset (numeric or NULL, optional) – observation-level offset, length-matched to y when non-NULL.

  • phi (numeric scalar, optional) – dispersion forwarded to tulpa_laplace() (used by negbin, gamma).

  • weights (numeric, optional; length length(y)) – per-observation likelihood weight, scaling that row's log-density, score and Fisher information. This is the channel a soft (fractional) latent label travels on; see the section below.

  • re_list, spatial (optional) – forwarded as-is.

  • control (list, optional) – on a block with a prior, entries merged over the driver's own tulpa_nested_laplace() control (n_threads, keep_grid_hessians = TRUE, diagnose_k = FALSE); an M-step fit is one iterate of the EM objective, so its outer Pareto-k diagnostic is off unless the block sets diagnose_k = TRUE.

spatial, re_list

Not consumed at the driver level – latent structure is per-submodel, set as a spatial / re_list field on each block m_step_encode() returns. Supplying either here is an error (rather than a silent no-op).

max_iter

Maximum EM iterations.

tol

Convergence tolerance on max relative parameter change.

damping

EM damping factor in [0, 1). With damping = d, the E-step weights are smoothed between iterations as (1 - d) * new + d * prev (d = 0 is no damping); the M-step then refits on the smoothed weights, so the parameter update is damped indirectly through the weights rather than by mixing successive parameter vectors.

correction

Post-EM correction. "none" returns the EM point estimate only. "mi" draws n_imputations independent hard z from the converged posterior weights P(z|y, theta_hat), refits each block on the hard z, and pools via rubins_pool(). "gibbs" runs true-density MH-within-Gibbs for n_gibbs sweeps starting from the EM fits, returning joint posterior draws. "auto" resolves to "none".

n_imputations

Number of MI draws (default 20L). Used when correction = "mi".

n_gibbs

Total Gibbs sweeps including warmup (default 2000L). Used when correction = "gibbs".

n_louis

Number of hard latent draws for the Monte Carlo estimate of the missing information in Louis' observed-information standard errors (default 1000L; 0 skips them). Each draw costs one m_step_encode() call and a score evaluation, no refit. See the section below.

draw_z

Optional function function(weights) -> hard_z that turns the E-step's continuous weights into a hard latent draw. Used by correction %in% c("mi", "gibbs") and by the Louis standard errors (n_louis). The default treats weights as a numeric vector of Bernoulli probabilities and draws per-observation. Multi-class / matrix-valued latent structures must supply their own callback.

m_step_extra

Optional function(fits, weights, ...) -> fits. Fired once per M-step in the EM iterations and MI draws. Receives the freshly assembled list of tulpa_laplace() results (fits), the continuous E-step weights P(z|y, theta) (NOT the hard z draw used by MI to encode the block), and any extra arguments forwarded through .... Returns a list with the same length and names as the input, possibly with mutated dispersion / shape / precision fields (e.g. fits[[k]]$phi). Use this to update non-eta parameters that fall out of the Laplace M-step (NB overdispersion, Gamma shape, Beta precision, Gaussian sigma). Gibbs correction requires NULL and fixed block hyperparameters.

beta_prior

Optional Gaussian prior on the fixed effects, applied to every block fit via tulpa_laplace() (i.e. blocks without a prior field). NULL (default) takes the engine default N(0, 2.5^2). Otherwise a list with sd (required) and optional mean; see tulpa_laplace(). The same prior flows into the MI / Gibbs correction refits, so penalized corrections come for free. A block may override the default by setting its own beta_prior field in m_step_encode (e.g. different priors for the occupancy and detection submodels). Use scalar mean / sd here when blocks differ in width; per-coefficient vectors belong on the block.

verbose

Print per-iteration progress.

log_complete

Optional function function(fits, z, ...) -> numeric returning log p(y, z, theta), with every complete-data likelihood normalizer, parameter prior and transformation Jacobian. Each block of fits carries the evaluated parameter vector in mode and its fixed effects in beta. The posterior evidence p(y) is unnecessary. NULL uses the engine density assembled from the complete-data GLMM blocks. The callback must be deterministic and return one finite value or -Inf. Used only with correction = "gibbs".

correction_control

List of Gibbs settings: warmup (default n_gibbs %/% 2L), thin (default 1L), mh_steps (conditional MH transitions per sweep, default 1L), and scale (t proposal scale inflation, default 1). Unknown entries are errors.

...

Forwarded to e_step, m_step_encode, and m_step_extra.

Value

A list with:

  • fits – named list of tulpa_laplace() results, one per block, each with beta and its complete-data se attached.

  • vcov, se, louis – for EM and MI, observed-information covariance and standard errors by Louis' method. For Gibbs, vcov is the full sampled parameter covariance and se the per-block fixed-effect posterior SDs; the EM information is in em_information.

  • weights – final E-step weights.

  • n_iter – number of EM iterations actually run.

  • converged – logical.

  • history – data.frame(iter, delta) of max relative parameter change per iteration.

  • correction – the resolved correction mode ("none", "mi", or "gibbs").

  • pooled – present when correction = "mi". Named list of pooled per-submodel summaries from rubins_pool().

  • draws – for MI, per-draw fit lists with beta / se. For Gibbs, a matrix of retained full parameter draws; column names identify the block, coefficient and random-effect group.

  • latent_draws, log_prob, final_fits – for Gibbs, latent states paired by row with draws, their complete-data log densities, and the final sampled parameters in E-step form. fits retains the EM initialization; converged describes that EM loop.

  • means, sds – Gibbs posterior means and SDs over retained draws.

  • accept_prob, mean_accept, draws_kind – for Gibbs, acceptance indicators for the conditional MH steps on retained sweeps, their mean, and "chain".

  • inference_mode, inference_tier, target – the actual inference class and target. Gibbs reports "exact", 1L, and "joint posterior p(theta, Z | y), conditional on fixed block hyperparameters".

Details

This is an engine block, not a front door: model packages call it programmatically, so its tuning knobs (max_iter, tol, damping) sit in the signature rather than in a control list.

Soft latent labels go in weights, not in y

The M-step maximizes the expected complete-data log-likelihood. For a Bernoulli latent z_i carrying E-step posterior weight w_i that is $$Q = \sum_i [\, w_i \log p_i + (1 - w_i) \log (1 - p_i) \,],$$ a weighted Bernoulli log-likelihood, which carries no binomial coefficient. Encode it as two rows per unit – y = 1 at weight w_i and y = 0 at weight 1 - w_i:

list(y       = rep(c(1, 0), each = n),
     X       = rbind(X, X),
     weights = c(w, 1 - w),
     family  = "binomial")

A fractional y on a binomial block is refused, and is not the same objective: it asks for the exact binomial density at a non-integer response, whose normalizer lchoose(n, y) is not zero there and depends on w. On the weighted encoding the block's log_marginal is the Laplace marginal of Q, an EM objective that increases across iterations.

Standard errors

Each entry of fits carries beta (the fixed effects) and se, read off that block's M-step curvature H_beta. That curvature is the complete-data information at the converged weights: it treats the latent labels as known, so these se understate the uncertainty by the information the latent variable withholds.

The observed-data information follows from Louis' (1982) identity, $$I_{obs}(\theta) = E[-\nabla^2 \ell_c(\theta; z) \mid y] - \mathrm{Var}[\nabla \ell_c(\theta; z) \mid y],$$ evaluated at the EM estimate. The first term is the blocks' H_beta (the M-step objective is the expected complete-data log-likelihood when the weights enter linearly, as in the weighted encoding below); the second, the missing information, is estimated from n_louis hard draws z ~ draw_z(weights), each encoded by m_step_encode() and scored at the estimate. The score covariance couples the blocks that share the latent variable, so vcov is one joint matrix across blocks. The result carries vcov (named "<block>:<coef>"), se (a named list per block) and louis (n_draws, and missing_fraction, the share of each coefficient's variance owed to the latent variable, 1 - se_complete^2 / se^2). It needs blocks without latent structure (re_list, spatial, prior), whose fixed effects are the whole parameter; otherwise, or when the estimated observed information is not positive definite, vcov and se are NULL and louis$unavailable says why. Dispersions set on a block (phi) are held at their values. The draws consume the random-number stream.

correction = "mi" targets the same quantity by refitting each draw and pooling with Rubin's rules. Its draws are taken at the fixed estimate, an improper imputation that leaves out the estimate's own uncertainty, so its pooled SE can run below the observed-information one.

Posterior sampling

correction = "gibbs" alternates an exact draw from p(Z | theta, y) with independence Metropolis-Hastings for p(theta | Z, y). Here theta contains every block's fixed effects and random-effect values. The complete-data Laplace mode and full latent precision define a multivariate-t proposal. The acceptance ratio uses the true complete-data density, including priors, divided by the proposal density at both parameter states. The current density is evaluated again after each latent update. The resulting chain has invariant joint posterior p(theta, Z | y) under the usual support and ergodicity conditions (Tanner and Wong, 1987; Robert and Casella, 1999). Finite chains require convergence and Monte Carlo diagnostics.

The engine density evaluates the native family likelihood, retaining normalizing constants, and normalized Gaussian coefficient and random-effect priors. It reads the hard complete-data blocks from m_step_encode(z, ...). These must encode every factor of p(y, z | theta), including the latent label model. Observation weights must be 0 or 1 on this path. Supply log_complete when the model needs additional factors or a different joint density. The callback replaces the entire density, including priors.

Complete-data blocks currently support fixed effects and any number of Gaussian random-effect terms with fixed covariance, including correlated slopes. Dispersion is fixed. Nested, spatial and custom-likelihood blocks are refused because their integrated fits supply no proposal for the full conditional parameter vector. Deterministic m_step_extra updates are refused on the Gibbs path. The parameter layout, coefficient order and random-effect group identities must remain fixed across latent draws.

During sampling the E-step receives per-block mode and beta containing the current parameter draw. It must use those values to compute the exact latent conditional of the same joint model as the density. A finite MCMC approximation to that conditional does not meet this contract. A separate unbiased-likelihood extended-state construction is one alternative when exact latent draws are unavailable (Andrieu and Roberts, 2009).

Each sweep costs one E-step, one complete-data Laplace solve per block, and 1 + correction_control$mh_steps joint-density evaluations. The proposal factorization covers the full parameter vector. MI costs one refit per block per imputation and retains the Tier 2 approximation.

Tier

"none" and "mi" are Tier 2. "gibbs" is Tier 1 for the declared joint posterior, conditional on the fixed dispersion and covariance.

References

Louis, T. A. (1982). Finding the observed information matrix when using the EM algorithm. JRSS B, 44(2), 226-233.

Tanner, M. A., and Wong, W. H. (1987). The calculation of posterior distributions by data augmentation. JASA, 82(398), 528-540. doi:10.1080/01621459.1987.10478458 .

Wei, G. C. G., and Tanner, M. A. (1990). A Monte Carlo implementation of the EM algorithm and the poor man's data augmentation algorithms. JASA, 85(411), 699-704. doi:10.1080/01621459.1990.10474930 .

Robert, C. P., and Casella, G. (1999). Monte Carlo Statistical Methods. Springer, sections 7.3.2-7.3.3. doi:10.1007/978-1-4757-3071-5 .

Andrieu, C., and Roberts, G. O. (2009). The pseudo-marginal approach for efficient Monte Carlo computations. Annals of Statistics, 37(2), 697-725. doi:10.1214/07-AOS574 .

Examples

# \donttest{
# Zero-inflated Poisson via EM: the E-step scores the posterior probability
# that each zero is non-structural. Those are soft labels, so the occupancy
# arm is the weighted Bernoulli above -- two rows per unit -- and the
# abundance arm weights each count by the same w.
set.seed(1)
n <- 200
z <- rbinom(n, 1, 0.7)
y <- rpois(n, 4) * z
X <- cbind(1, rnorm(n))

e_step <- function(fits, ...) {
  if (!length(fits)) return(list(weights = pmax(as.numeric(y > 0), 0.5)))
  psi <- plogis(drop(X %*% fits$occ$mode))
  lam <- exp(drop(X %*% fits$abund$mode))
  w <- ifelse(y > 0, 1, psi * exp(-lam) / (psi * exp(-lam) + (1 - psi)))
  list(weights = w)
}
m_step_encode <- function(weights, ...) {
  list(
    occ   = list(y = rep(c(1, 0), each = n), X = rbind(X, X),
                 weights = c(weights, 1 - weights), family = "binomial"),
    abund = list(y = y, X = X, family = "poisson", weights = weights)
  )
}

res <- tulpa_em_laplace(e_step, m_step_encode, verbose = FALSE)
res$converged
#> [1] TRUE
plogis(res$fits$occ$mode[1])    # P(non-structural), truth 0.7
#> [1] 0.7034743
exp(res$fits$abund$mode[1])     # abundance mean, truth 4
#> [1] 3.871112
# }
